2.3. Markov Dynamics. If (X,B) is a measurable space and U is a topological space, a stochastic kernel P from U to X is a function P : U × B → + with the property that u  → P(u,B) is Borel measurable for each B ∈ B and B  → P(u,B) is a probability on (X,B) for all u ∈ U. When U = X, we say that P is a stochastic kernel on X. Given a stochastic kernel P from U to X, we set (Ph)(u) := h(x′)P(u,dx′) (h ∈ bmX, u ∈ U). When X is a topological space we use the following standard terminology: We call P Feller if Ph is continuous on U whenever h ∈ bmX is continuous on X.
